caveats: All results were measured on Linux with NVIDIA GPUs and don't carry over to other operating systems or hardware. On macOS, AlphaLlama runs its standard Metal build: the newer engine backend measured here, and its speed-ups, need an NVIDIA GPU.
Formats differ by engine (labelled on each bar); NVFP4 is emulated below Blackwell.

Exact decoding (output identical to the engine's standard greedy decode; lossless drafting such as verified MTP is allowed) is ranked whether or not it reproduces bit-for-bit across restarts; runs that didn't reproduce carry a badge. Other engines' exact runs weren't restart-checked.

RTX 4070 Laptop power settings, unchanged for every engine: GPU power limit 55 W (the stock default; up to 140 W allowed, plus up to 25 W firmware dynamic boost), firmware performance profile, on AC power, Linux. CPU (Core i9-14900HX) limits 140 W, but a cooling fault held it at about 0.55-1.4 GHz, below its 2.2 GHz base, with thermal throttling on every prompt, so every engine is slower there than on a healthy laptop (most for work kept in system memory); comparisons within that machine still hold. Average GPU power during the run: AlphaLlama 37-45 W, Ollama 14-30 W.
All three prompt sets are scored, including the headline (R) tasks. Some engine settings were tuned on the R and V prompts; that is disclosed, not hidden.

RTX 5090: AlphaLlama's and NInfer's speeds were timed by each engine's own command-line tool; the other engines went through the shared streaming client. Their 5090 rows are shown and ranked with that note, but aren't used as speed records or peak speeds (the same rule that keeps the RTX 3090 1,153 tok/s CLI figure off the records) until a shared-client re-run.
FreeToken on the 5090 and 3090 ran its pip + auto configuration, not its tuned path; the 4080 row is its tuned path.

Ollama versions differ by GPU: 0.40.11 on the RTX 3090 and 4080 (re-run 2026-10-27/28), older on the 5090 and the 4070 laptop. 0.40.11 is much faster than the older builds: about 1.6x on the 3090 and 3.6x on the 4080, where it splits the 35B model between GPU and system memory far better.

AlphaLlama on the RTX 3090 (newer engine backend): 35B ran at a 32,768-token context, where its exact output matches its plain decode (at the default 98,304 it doesn't yet; being fixed). 27B ran on a batch-invariant build, which isn't the standard release, at a 131,072-token context with q4_0 KV; its speed there is within 2.4% of the default 262,144-token context. Speed and identity come from the same configuration for each model.

AlphaLlama on Qwen3.8-27B, RTX 4080 (newer engine backend): the model only fits in 16 GB with some layers and the token embeddings on the CPU side, and there its verified-MTP mode matched plain decoding only 1 of 4 times, so it's on the fast board. Its plain decoding is on the board as exact output; all three modes ran in the same configuration.

Flash-Next (RTX 4080 and RTX 5090): AlphaLlama's release candidate 3e82a70ea and Strata 0.2.8 ran in one window per machine (on the RTX 5090 Strata used its fastest, tuned setup), 2 passes with the second reversed, a fresh server per engine. Flash-Next has no exact mode with drafting on AlphaLlama, so its exact row is plain decoding. Earlier AlphaLlama builds had a Flash-Next bug that could emit stray tokens in long outputs; this build has the fix and no output had any. The RTX 3090 Flash-Next results are being re-run and will be added when they're ready.

records.rule: A record is an engine's best single-prompt decode speed: the median of at least 2 passes that agree within 10%, measured with the shared streaming client. Any prompt set, any mode; fast modes are labelled. Speeds timed by an engine's own command-line tool are not records.
